## TL;DR

The four Checks tabs navigated successfully in component interaction coverage. Review identified an app lifecycle defect: the page left its five-second local-slot poll running after unmount. I now clear that interval during teardown, and a fake-timer regression test confirms no further `/api/local-check-slots` request occurs after unmount. The original slowdown remains unattributed. A live visual pass at desktop and phone widths was unavailable because the browser access host could not be reached. The final scoped RepoOS check passed after formatting the test.

## Work and rationale

I inspected the task and Checks view implementation. Its sections are buttons in a tablist, with each click updating the route query. The page polls active checks every three seconds and local check slot holders every five seconds. The active-check poll already stored its timer id and cleared it during `onBeforeUnmount`; the local-slot poll did neither. Every mount could therefore leave another five-second timer and retain a component closure after navigating away.

The click-through test switches among Now, Runs, Test suite and Check plan without screenshots. Each route query and selected tab updates as expected, and no navigation hang occurs. During review, the lifecycle code was examined and the missing cleanup was identified. I added a timer handle for the local-slot poll and clear it in the existing unmount hook alongside the active-check poll.

The fake-timer regression test mounts the Checks view, records local-slot API requests, unmounts the view, advances time past the polling period and confirms the request count stays unchanged. This checks the leak’s effect directly without relying on total timer counts that can include unrelated view timers. The sequential tab test now names the missing tab in its assertion failure.

I added an “Investigation outcome” section to the task through RepoOS. The current board copy records the fixed poll leak, the click-through result, and the limits of the browser verification.

## Approaches tried

- Inspected the Checks view lifecycle hooks and compared the local-slot interval with the already-cleaned active-check poll.
- Attempted live browser access through the computer-use integration. The browser access host was unavailable before a page could be opened.
- Ran the sequential tab click test and the fake-timer teardown test. Both pass.
- Ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. A first run found a formatting issue; I ran `bun run fmt` and repeated the scoped check. The final run passed remote build and tests, the headless browser gate, and local formatting, lint, build, contrast, CSS, artifact and UI smoke checks.

## Challenges and blockers

The browser access host was unavailable, so I could not inspect the page at 1440px, 390px or 320px in both themes. Component-level route assertions and the headless smoke gate do not establish those layouts. Direct tab navigation did not hang, and the poll leak was real, but the evidence does not prove that the leak caused the reported slowdown or that the capture harness was responsible. One app-side accumulation defect is fixed; the original performance attribution and live visual matrix remain unverified.

## Key learnings

Repeated SPA navigation can expose teardown bugs even when individual interactions work normally. A page may continue polling after it disappears without blocking the immediate navigation sequence. For this issue class, a regression test should advance time after unmount and assert the affected request no longer occurs. A passing headless smoke test is useful general coverage, but it does not replace a live multi-width, multi-theme visual review.
